title: Onboarding certification runbook and runtime compatibility guardrail
creator: Priya Patel
description: Goal: Create an operational certification runbook, lightweight ledger artifact, and telemetry contract that together enable safe publishing and maintenance of Redwood-verified performance claims for newly onboarded model versions. This ticket defines the acceptance criteria, tasks, and rollout plan needed to reduce onboarding time while ensuring latency/throughput/cost claims are reproducible across runtime variants and hardware anchors.
acceptance_criteria: A single runbook (Confluence) exists describing step-by-step certification including data sources, synthetic harness commands, and pass/fail thresholds for latency, throughput, and cost.

A simple signed ledger artifact (git-backed JSON + checksum) is produced by the onboarding pipeline containing measured 95th/median latency, tokens/sec throughput, and normalized cost-per-token for canonical anchors.

Telemetry contract documented and implemented: required traces, histograms, and metrics emitted by runtime for continuous verification (latency_p95_ms, token_out_per_s, kv_cache_hit_rate, cost_estimate_usd_per_1k_tokens).
A test harness job runs in CI and verifies a sampled production shadow invocation reproduces published numbers within tolerances or surfaces a failed certification triage ticket.
Runbook reviewed and approved by runtime eng lead and observability PM; accessible to Solutions and SRE at read/write roles.
Automated PR in onboarding pipeline generates ledger artifact and attaches a link to generated telemetry snapshots in the build output.
Security checklist completed for artifacts (no customer data, KMS-signed release metadata where applicable).
tasks: Draft runbook: steps, expected commands, required artifacts (logs, traces, sample prompts)
Define canonical anchor hardware + model variant matrix for certification runs
Add telemetry contract to runtime telemetry registry and instrument missing metrics
Implement ledger generator in onboarding pipeline (github: redwood/inference-onboard/actions/ledger-gen)
Add CI job that executes sample workloads and compares results against ledger tolerances
Create RBAC page and retention policy for generated artifacts
Run two manual certifications (one open model, one quantized variant) and collect lessons learned
updates: 2025-01-10: Created ticket. Initial scoping meeting with runtime, observability, and DX. Agreed high-level outputs: runbook, ledger artifact, telemetry contract.
2025-01-22: Runtime team prototype for telemetry metrics completed (ENG-2210). Missing: cost normalization formula. Action: PM to coordinate cost normalization doc.
2025-01-28: Draft runbook posted to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ONBOARD/Certification+Runbook+Draft. Requesting review from Ayla Chen (runtime) and Liam O'Connor (SRE).

2025-02-03: Review notes from Ayla: recommend adding KV cache warmup step and explicit empty-cache baseline. Liam requested inclusion of synthetic tail-latency spike test and guidance for sample sizes.

2025-02-07: Implemented ledger-gen action prototype: https://github.com/redwood/inference-onboard/pull/214 (WIP). It outputs ledger.json with keys: model_id, hw_anchor, median_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, tokens_per_sec, cost_usd_per_1k_tokens, checksum.
2025-02-12: Observability PM Marta Kovacs asked to include latency histogram buckets and suggested using OpenTelemetry semantic conventions. Updated telemetry contract accordingly.

2025-02-15: Ran first manual certification against open model gptx-3b on A100 anchor. Results captured and ledger draft attached to the Confluence runbook. Noted p95 deviation of +12% vs historical anchor — flagged for follow-up (see risks).
risks: Anchor drift: hardware performance differences across cloud regions could make published numbers unstable — mitigations: normalize to a hardware baseline and include hardware fingerprint in ledger.

Cost normalization ambiguity: differences in GPU pricing and utilization models may lead to misleading cost-per-token claims — mitigation: publish raw token/sec + reference cost formula and link to pricing inputs.
False confidence from small sample sizes: build CI job to run adequate samples and surface variance statistics.
Automation errors: faulty ledger generator could publish incorrect checksums — require signed artifacts + CI gate that verifies checksums.
Operational burden: too many manual steps in certification will slow onboarding; prioritize reducing to minimal automated subset for most models.
test_plan: CI job that replays a deterministic set of prompts against the onboarded model on the canonical hardware anchor with cold and warmed KV cache runs.
Compare median and p95 latency within tolerance (±10% median, ±15% p95) and tokens/sec within ±12%.
Verify ledger checksum matches generated artifact and that build publishes link to trace snapshot in observability dashboard.
Run canary: when ledger mismatch occurs, open an automated triage ticket assigned to runtime on-call with attached artifacts.
notes: Next step: align on final tolerance thresholds in cross-functional meeting (scheduled 2025-02-20).
Follow-up: prototype a lightweight ‘certify --quick’ mode for fast developer feedback that runs a subset of checks.
Long term: consider migrating ledger artifacts to signed git tags and exposing a read-only registry for downstream teams.
